limitations: Existing metrics/system JSONL plus completed result.json (subsequently authorized); no native-summary/private/state/env copied.
Cross-stage windows approximate early formal phase and are not identical durations or a controlled causal comparison.
Stage metrics are collected sequentially across a reported sampleDurationMs; 1s process samples cannot explain sub-second stalls.
CPU percentages use 100% per logical CPU. Parent/cgroup/process scopes overlap and must not be summed.
No CPU MHz/frequency, host thermal/power state, physical disk latency, exact sender trace or isolated EDGE ACK timing in these sources.
Do not attribute failure to ext4 based on one rerun or infer hardware ceiling from average CPU.
Original 7k PASS is historical single-run success, not reproducible stable-platform proof after this 7k failure.

hostContext.scope: Parent reported a later idle Windows sample, not read independently here.
hostContext.conclusion: WSL cpuset does not reserve host physical CPUs; later Windows process CPU cannot identify the cause of earlier failure. A new simultaneous host/guest sample is required.
hostContext.cpuFrequencyEvidence: Absent from these archived guest samples. Cannot infer sustained clocks, throttling by host, thermals or power limits.

conclusions: The new 7000 QPS run failed after 10.228s formal work; historical single 7000 QPS PASS is not a reproducible stable platform.
In compared coarse intervals, EDGE whole-send mean from cumulative differences grows about 3.18x and queue grows strongly; this is the clearest changed progress indicator.
Redirect allocation and GC pause accumulation are similar in old/new 7k intervals. Current data does not support a large new stop-the-world increase.
Guest CPU averages, zero recorded cgroup quota throttling, and Java producer native latency do not prove whole-node resource exhaustion or an isolated Kafka broker bottleneck.
File location is not established as causal; host/guest scheduling and EDGE-specific send steps require simultaneous evidence.
